# Format STAT 432 Homework Plots

Apply these rules only after an explicit request to improve a homework plot. Keep the plot's data, statistical meaning, and analysis unchanged; focus on presentation.

- Leave enough margin for the title, axis labels, tick labels, and legend. Prevent clipping and avoid excess empty space.
- Use a short, informative title that describes what is plotted. Avoid oversized titles.
- Label both axes with the variable or quantity and include units when relevant. Use readable tick marks and ranges that make comparisons clear without distorting the data.
- Use concise legend labels that identify groups or methods. Include a legend only when multiple series or groups need explanation.
- Choose a small, color-vision-accessible palette with clearly distinguishable series. Do not rely on color alone; also vary point shapes or line types when useful.
- Set figure dimensions and text sizes deliberately so labels, points, lines, and legends remain legible in the rendered homework document. Use the plotting system's native controls in R or Python, and check the final rendered output when available.
- Preserve the surrounding code style and make the smallest focused changes needed. Do not change the analysis, add decorative effects, or introduce plot dependencies just for styling.
